summary: Nine-lens review of the merged Phase 9-12 code, each finding adversarially verified

confirmed.title: Any app can open the vault without the PIN: the exported MainActivity navigates to whatever route `gs_route` names
confirmed.detail: Phase 11's GsAppEffects reads the `gs_route` string extra from MainActivity's launch intent and from every new intent, with no validation. Once Home is current it calls `navController.navigate(route)`. MainActivity is exported and needs no permission, so any installed app or intent-launcher app can open it with `gs_route=vault_media`. After Splash and Home, VaultMediaScreen opens, and it has no lock check of its own. The same path works with `gs_route=vault/recovery_question`: that screen writes new security answers (`setThreeSecurityQuestions`) and then opens VaultMedia, so an attacker can take over the vault reset too. A route that is not in the graph makes `navigate` throw IllegalArgumentException, so any app can also crash the app. Phase 10 guarded its own `floating_route` extra against exactly this attack; Phase 11's extra has no such guard.
confirmed.evidence: GsPermissions.kt:170 `private fun Intent.takeGsRoute(): String? = getStringExtra(EXTRA_GS_ROUTE)?.also { removeExtra(EXTRA_GS_ROUTE) }`; :182 `var pending by remember { mutableStateOf(activity.intent?.takeGsRoute()) }`; :184 the onNewIntent listener does the same; :201 `else -> navController.navigate(route) { launchSingleTop = true }`. AndroidManifest.xml:70-73 declares MainActivity `exported="true"` with no permission. GalleryNavHost.kt:366 `composable(Screen.VaultMedia.route) { VaultMediaScreen(...) }` has no lock gate. MainActivity.kt:61-63 shows the guard Phase 10 used: "This activity is exported, so only a sidebar tool's own route is accepted (never e.g. vault_media past the lock)". Repro: `adb shell am start -n com.quizango.gallery/.MainActivity --es gs_route vault_media` opens the private vault grid without the PIN, and `--es gs_route x` crashes the app.
confirmed.reasoning:
I could not refute this. The finding stands. Evidence at HEAD:
- GsPermissions.kt:170 reads the `gs_route` extra with no check: `getStringExtra(EXTRA_GS_ROUTE)?.also { removeExtra(...) }`.
- :182 and :184 take that value from both the launch intent and every new intent.
- Once the current route is Home, :201 calls `navController.navigate(route) { launchSingleTop = true }` for any value other than GS_ROUTE_PERMISSION or Home.
- AndroidManifest.xml:71-72 declares MainActivity `exported="true"` with no permission, and it has a MAIN/LAUNCHER filter, so an explicit intent from any app reaches it.
- MainActivity.accept() (lines 107-116) only looks at deep-link, notification and shortcut extras. It never strips or checks `gs_route`. GsAppEffects runs no matter what, because GalleryNavHost.kt:94 always composes it.
- Screen.kt:47 defines VaultMedia as "vault_media". GalleryNavHost.kt:366-372 composes VaultMediaScreen with no lock gate. The only lock is the separate VaultLock destination (:362), which reaches VaultMedia through its own navigate at :430.
- VaultRecoveryQuestion ("vault/recovery_question", :408) can also be reached directly.
- An unknown route makes NavController.navigate throw IllegalArgumentException inside the LaunchedEffect, which crashes the app.
- Phase 10 guards its own extra against exactly this case (MainActivity.kt:60-63 and `isSidebarRoute` in FloatingTool.kt:68). Phase 11 has no such guard.
- 11-SUMMARY.md:44 describes `gs_route` only as the way Quick Info and the IU screen open routes. It records no deliberate deviation.

The legitimate senders are few:
- GsLaunch.kt:82 sends GS_ROUTE_PERMISSION.
- InstallUninstallActivity.kt:97 sends Screen.VaultLock.route.
- QuickInfoActivity.kt:167/169 sends Screen.Home.route and Screen.Settings.route.
- QuickInfoActivity.kt:179/311 sends album routes from gsAlbumRoute or Screen.AlbumDetail.createRoute.
- gsAlbumRoute may also yield Favorites, Moments or CollageMaker routes, as the reviewer listed. Confirm that when writing the fix.

Severity stays critical: any installed app can open the vault without the PIN, overwrite the recovery answers, and crash the app.

confirmed.title: Exported MainActivity opens any route named in the gs_route extra (vault PIN bypass, crash)
confirmed.detail:
GsAppEffects runs inside every GalleryNavHost. It reads EXTRA_GS_ROUTE ("gs_route") from MainActivity's launch intent and from every new intent. For any value other than gs_permission or home it calls navController.navigate(route) with no check. MainActivity is exported (it is the launcher), so anyone can set this extra: any installed app, an intent-launcher app, adb, or a browsable intent:// link (package=com.quizango.gallery;S.gs_route=...) that matches the BROWSABLE deep-link filter.

Vault bypass: with gs_route=vault_media the app goes Splash -> Home -> VaultMediaScreen. That screen has no lock check of its own. The vault key is a Keystore key that is not tied to the PIN (VaultCrypto.keystoreKey sets no user-auth requirement), so the decrypted private media shows without the PIN. vault/settings and vault/recovery_question are open the same way. Setting a new recovery answer there lets an attacker reset the PIN later through Forgot password.

Crash: any route that is not in the graph (e.g. gs_route=x) makes navigate() throw IllegalArgumentException inside the LaunchedEffect, which crashes the app.

The other outside inputs are allowlisted: floating_route through isSidebarRoute, route through shortcutEntry, deep links through deepLinkEntry. gs_route is not.
confirmed.evidence:
GsPermissions.kt:170 `private fun Intent.takeGsRoute(): String? = getStringExtra(EXTRA_GS_ROUTE)?.also { removeExtra(EXTRA_GS_ROUTE) }`
:182 `var pending by remember { mutableStateOf(activity.intent?.takeGsRoute()) }`
:184 is the onNewIntent listener.
:198-202 `when (route) { GS_ROUTE_PERMISSION -> permissionFlow(); Screen.Home.route -> Unit; else -> navController.navigate(route) { launchSingleTop = true } }`
GalleryNavHost.kt:366 `composable(Screen.VaultMedia.route) { VaultMediaScreen(...) }` has no gate.
VaultCrypto.kt:29-45 builds the KeyGenParameterSpec without setUserAuthenticationRequired.
Repro: `adb shell am start -n com.quizango.gallery/.MainActivity --es gs_route vault_media`
confirmed.fix: In GsPermissions.kt, make takeGsRoute keep only the values GsLaunch's callers actually send, and drop everything else. For example: `getStringExtra(EXTRA_GS_ROUTE)?.also { removeExtra(EXTRA_GS_ROUTE) }?.takeIf { it == GS_ROUTE_PERMISSION || it in GS_ALLOWED_ROUTES }`. GS_ALLOWED_ROUTES is the set of non-vault routes that Quick Info, the IU screen and the Quick Info disabled notification pass; check the GsLaunch.kt:38 callers to build it. It must never include vault_media, vault/settings or vault/recovery_question. If vault is ever needed, map it to Screen.VaultLock.route. Also wrap line 201 in `runCatching { navController.navigate(route) { launchSingleTop = true } }` so an unknown route cannot crash the app.
confirmed.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. The code at HEAD matches it.

1. **Unchecked route.** GsPermissions.kt:170 reads the "gs_route" extra with no check. Lines 182 and 184 take it from the launch intent and from every new intent. Line 201 passes any value other than gs_permission or home straight to `navController.navigate(route)`.
2. **Reachable from outside.** GsAppEffects runs for every NavHost (GalleryNavHost.kt:94).
3. **Open entry point.** MainActivity is exported (AndroidManifest.xml:71-72) and has LAUNCHER, PICK/GET_CONTENT and a BROWSABLE VIEW filter. Any app, a launcher or intent-shortcut app, or adb can set the extra.
4. **Other inputs are checked.** MainActivity.accept/openEntry filters deep links, notification actions and shortcut routes (MainActivity.kt:107-130). Nothing checks gs_route.
5. **Only the app's own senders use it.** EXTRA_GS_ROUTE is written only by GsLaunch.kt:38.
6. **No gate on the vault screens.**
   - Screen.VaultMedia is "vault_media" (Screen.kt:47).
   - Its destination at GalleryNavHost.kt:366-373 renders VaultMediaScreen with no lock check, and VaultMediaScreen itself has no lock logic.
   - VaultSetting ("vault/settings") and VaultRecoveryQuestion ("vault/recovery_question") have no gate either.
   - The PIN is enforced only by navigating through VaultLock or VaultLockFor.
7. **Key not tied to the PIN.** VaultCrypto.kt:34 builds the KeyGenParameterSpec with no setUserAuthenticationRequired, so decryption works without the PIN.
8. **Bypass works.** The pending route waits until Home is current (lines 190-196), then navigates. `--es gs_route vault_media` therefore shows the decrypted vault without the PIN.
9. **Crash.** A route not in the graph makes navigate() throw IllegalArgumentException inside a LaunchedEffect with no runCatching, which crashes the app.

None of the phase summaries records this as a deliberate deviation. The 2.7.2 reference only sends its own fixed "key_notification_intent" values, so nothing in the reference requires an open route channel.

**Severity: major rather than critical.** Exploiting it takes a crafted intent: another app, adb, an intent-launcher, or a browser intent:// link. A background app cannot see the screen. Still, it defeats the vault PIN against exactly the person it protects against, someone holding the unlocked phone. Planting a recovery answer through vault/recovery_question also gives a lasting PIN reset path.

confirmed.title: Pro screen crashes on open: painterResource on a layer-list drawable
confirmed.detail: The paywall slider draws its banner with painterResource(R.drawable.sub_ic_mask_anim). That drawable is a <layer-list> (a shape plus a <bitmap>), not a vector. In Compose UI 1.7.8, painterResource throws IllegalArgumentException("Only VectorDrawables and rasterized asset types are supported ex. PNG, JPG, WEBP") for any XML whose root is not <vector>. HorizontalPager composes page 0 as soon as ProScreen opens, so every way into Pro crashes the app: the Settings Go Ads Free banner, Home's always-present AD_FREE top-bar slot (HomeShell.kt:70/126) and the PayWallActivity deep link.
confirmed.evidence: res/drawable/sub_ic_mask_anim.xml starts with <layer-list>. The APK's META-INF/androidx.compose.ui_ui.version is 1.7.8. In ui-android-1.7.8-sources PainterResources.android.kt, loadVectorResource has `if (parser.seekToStartTag().name != "vector") throw IllegalArgumentException(errorMessage)`. A scan of the whole app found only two painterResource calls on non-vector XML, this one and SettingsScreen.kt:314, both added in Phase 9. Every other shape or layer-list goes through Modifier.drawableBackground.
confirmed.fix: ProScreen.kt:240-248: replace the Image with Box(Modifier.fillMaxWidth().aspectRatio(3f / 2f).clip(RoundedCornerShape(8.sdp)).background(colorResource(R.color.lib_white_for_slider)).drawableBackground(R.drawable.sub_ic_mask_anim)). This uses the existing helper from ui.home, which ProScreen.kt already imports.
confirmed.reasoning:
The finding is confirmed, so I could not refute it.

1. ProScreen.kt:241 calls painterResource(R.drawable.sub_ic_mask_anim) inside the HorizontalPager item lambda (line 237). The pager always composes page 0, so this runs as soon as the screen opens.
2. The only copy of the resource is app/src/main/res/drawable/sub_ic_mask_anim.xml. There is no PNG or qualified variant. Its root element is <layer-list> (a shape plus a <bitmap>).
3. libs.versions.toml sets composeBom = 2025.02.00, which resolves to ui-android 1.7.8 (that jar is in the Gradle cache). In its PainterResources.android.kt, line 69 sends any path ending in .xml to the vector loader. Lines 98-99 then throw IllegalArgumentException when the root tag is not "vector".
4. Nothing guards the call: there is no try/catch, and no other code path draws this drawable.

Result: opening Pro crashes every time, whichever way the user gets there.

I did not check the second site the reviewer named (SettingsScreen.kt:314, ic_red_dot). The house helper Modifier.drawableBackground exists (HomeSelection.kt:227) and ProScreen.kt already imports it (line 66, used at line 170), so the proposed fix is valid.

confirmed.title: Settings crashes whenever a row's red dot shows: painterResource on a <shape>
confirmed.detail: SettingRow draws the attention dot with Image(painterResource(R.drawable.ic_red_dot)). ic_red_dot is an oval <shape>, so Compose 1.7.8 throws IllegalArgumentException as soon as any row has dot = true. The IU row (shown when `campaign`) has dot = !canDrawOverlays. The GS row (shown when campaign && online) has dot = !(phoneGranted && canDrawOverlays), which is always true (see the CALL_PHONE finding). InstallSource.isCampaign returns true for every debug build and for every install without an organic referrer (sideloads, no Play referrer). For those users, opening Settings while online, or without the overlay permission, crashes the app once the campaign LaunchedEffect recomposes the rows.
confirmed.evidence: res/drawable/ic_red_dot.xml: `<shape android:shape="oval">`, and there is no vector variant in any qualifier. SettingsScreen.kt:313-320: `if (dot) Image(painter = painterResource(R.drawable.ic_red_dot), ...)`. PainterResources.android.kt (1.7.8) throws when the XML root is not "vector". InstallSource.kt:28 returns true when FLAG_DEBUGGABLE is set, and classify() treats a null referrer as CAMPAIGN.
confirmed.fix: In SettingRow (SettingsScreen.kt:313-320), replace the Image with `if (dot) Box(Modifier.align(Alignment.TopEnd).offset(x = if (dotCentered) 4.sdp else 0.dp, y = (-4).sdp).size(8.sdp).drawableBackground(R.drawable.ic_red_dot))`. Then grep the rest of the code for other painterResource calls on <shape> drawables.
confirmed.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. It holds at HEAD.

1. The drawable is a shape, not a vector. res/drawable/ic_red_dot.xml has `<shape android:shape="oval">` as its root, and it is the only ic_red_dot file in res. No qualifier folder has a vector or raster version.

2. SettingsScreen.kt:313-320 runs `if (dot) Image(painter = painterResource(R.drawable.ic_red_dot), ...)`. The project uses Compose BOM 2025.02.00 (gradle/libs.versions.toml:13), which gives ui 1.7.8. In that version, painterResource sends any .xml drawable to the vector loader. The loader throws IllegalArgumentException ("Only VectorDrawables and rasterized asset types are supported") when the root tag is not `vector`.

3. The crash is easy to reach:
   - `campaign` is set by a LaunchedEffect (line 164) from InstallSource.isCampaign.
   - isCampaign returns true whenever FLAG_DEBUGGABLE is set (InstallSource.kt, first line of isCampaign).
   - classify() treats a null or non-organic referrer as CAMPAIGN, which covers sideloads and installs where the referrer lookup times out.
   - Line 224 shows the IU row whenever `campaign` is true, with `dot = !canDrawOverlays`. Overlay permission is off by default, so the dot shows.
   - Line 212 shows the GS row when `campaign && online`, with `dot = !(phoneGranted && canDrawOverlays)`.

   So every debug build crashes on opening Settings unless overlay permission is already granted. Real campaign or sideload installs crash too.

4. Nothing else guards or catches this. The 09 and 10 phase summaries were not opened in this pass, but a decision recorded there could not make a guaranteed crash safe.

5. The suggested fix uses existing code. drawableBackground is already imported (SettingsScreen.kt:82) and already used for shape backgrounds at lines 275 and 396.

confirmed.title: The sidebar's Quick Access Settings gear opens Splash and Home instead of the Floating settings screen
confirmed.detail: The settings button in the sidebar panel's All tools card sends `floating_route=floating_setting` through `FloatingButtons.routeIntent`. MainActivity keeps that extra only if `isSidebarRoute(route)` is true. That function accepts only routes that some FloatingTool opens, and no tool opens `floating_setting`, so the extra is dropped. The app then restarts (CLEAR_TASK) at Splash and lands on Home, and the Quick Access Settings screen never opens. In 2.7.2 this button opens FloatingSettingActivity (bo/s; Phase 10 summary: "panel settings button = FloatingSettingActivity").
confirmed.evidence: SidebarPanel.kt:271-274 `fun openSettings() { close(); start(FloatingButtons.routeIntent(context, Screen.FloatingSetting.route)) }`. FloatingTool.kt:69-70 `fun isSidebarRoute(route: String): Boolean = FloatingTool.entries.any { route == it.route(junkCleanedToday = true) || route == it.route(junkCleanedToday = false) }`, and `FloatingTool.route()` (54-66) never returns "floating_setting". MainActivity.kt:62-63 `?.takeIf { pick == null && isSidebarRoute(it) }` gives null, so line 87 picks `startRoute = Screen.Splash.route` and nothing navigates.
confirmed.fix: FloatingTool.kt:69-70: `fun isSidebarRoute(route: String): Boolean = route == Screen.FloatingSetting.route || FloatingTool.entries.any { route == it.route(junkCleanedToday = true) || route == it.route(junkCleanedToday = false) }` (also update the KDoc to mention the panel settings button), and add `assertTrue(isSidebarRoute(Screen.FloatingSetting.route))` in FloatingSidebarTest.kt next to lines 140-142.
confirmed.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. Every link in the chain checks out at HEAD.
1. SidebarPanel.kt:271-274: openSettings() calls FloatingButtons.routeIntent(context, Screen.FloatingSetting.route).
2. Screen.kt:145: that route is "floating_setting".
3. FloatingButtons.kt:32-34: routeIntent sets NEW_TASK|CLEAR_TASK and puts EXTRA_ROUTE.
4. MainActivity.kt:62-63 reads the extra but keeps it only when `pick == null && isSidebarRoute(it)`.
5. FloatingTool.kt:54-66: FloatingTool.route() never returns "floating_setting". The SETTINGS tool maps to Screen.Settings, not FloatingSetting. So isSidebarRoute (69-70) returns false and floatingRoute is null.
6. MainActivity.kt:87 then uses startRoute = Splash, and the navigate at line 89 is skipped.
7. accept(intent) does not handle EXTRA_ROUTE either, so nothing else catches it.

Result: the task is cleared and the app restarts at Splash, then Home, and the Quick Access Settings screen never opens.

The 10-SUMMARY.md lines 35-36 record "panel settings button = FloatingSettingActivity" as the intended behaviour, not as a deviation. FloatingSidebarTest.kt:140-146 has no assert for FloatingSetting.

Allowing this route is safe. FloatingSetting holds only the Always ON/OFF toggle, and Home already reaches it through navigateOnce (GalleryNavHost.kt:800-801). No vault or other guarded screen is exposed.

I am keeping the severity at major: one sidebar control does the wrong thing, but it does not crash and loses no data. I did not run the app on a device, and I did not re-check the reference smali for bo/s. I relied on the phase summary's statement about 2.7.2.

confirmed.title: USER_PRESENT receiver is registered not-exported, so Quick Info never opens after unlock
confirmed.detail:
When a call ends while the screen is locked (CallEndAction.WAIT_FOR_UNLOCK), the receiver posts the "Conversation ended" notification. It also registers a runtime USER_PRESENT receiver that should open Quick Info 300 ms after unlock.

USER_PRESENT is sent by SystemUI's KeyguardViewMediator. SystemUI runs under its own app uid, not the system uid, so the receiver can never get it:
- On API 33+, a RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED receiver only gets broadcasts from the system uid or from the app itself; the platform reports anything else as "Exported Denial".
- On API 24-32, ContextCompat registers the receiver with the broadcast permission com.quizango.gallery.DYNAMIC_RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED_PERMISSION. That permission is signature-level (see the merged manifest), and SystemUI does not hold it.

Result: on every API level Quick Info never appears after unlocking, and with notifications off nothing appears at all. 2.7.2 shows it. The package-change receiver in PackageMonitorService is not affected, because those broadcasts come from system_server.
confirmed.evidence:
GsSetupCardReceiver.kt:89 `ContextCompat.registerReceiver(app, receiver, IntentFilter(Intent.ACTION_USER_PRESENT), ContextCompat.RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED)`
Merged debug manifest: `<permission android:name="com.quizango.gallery.DYNAMIC_RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED_PERMISSION" android:protectionLevel="signature" />`
Reference GsSetupCardReceiver.smali:1416-1425: IntentFilter("android.intent.action.USER_PRESENT") is passed to t2/b.OooO0O0.
t2/b.smali:620-679: on SDK >= 33 it calls h3/l.BsUTWEAMAI, which is registerReceiver(r, f, null, null, 0x2), i.e. RECEIVER_EXPORTED. On 26-32 it passes flags 0; below 26 it registers with no permission.
confirmed.fix: In GsSetupCardReceiver.kt:89, change ContextCompat.RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED to ContextCompat.RECEIVER_EXPORTED and keep everything else as is. This matches 2.7.2 (flag 0x2 on API 33+, plain registration before that). It is safe because USER_PRESENT is a protected broadcast that only the platform can send. Add a one-line comment saying why: SystemUI, not the system uid, sends USER_PRESENT, so a not-exported receiver never gets it.
confirmed.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. It stands.

1. The code at HEAD matches the claim. E:/Gallery/app/src/main/java/com/quizango/gallery/ui/gs/GsSetupCardReceiver.kt:89 registers the USER_PRESENT receiver with ContextCompat.RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED. It is reached from WAIT_FOR_UNLOCK at lines 60-62.

2. The reference claim is accurate.
- Reference GsSetupCardReceiver.smali:1416-1425 builds IntentFilter("android.intent.action.USER_PRESENT") and passes it to t2/b.OooO0O0.
- t2/b.OooO0O0 calls h3/l.BsUTWEAMAI on SDK >= 33 (0x21). That method calls registerReceiver(r, f, null, null, 0x2); 0x2 is RECEIVER_EXPORTED.
- On SDK 26-32 it calls h3/l.DxDJysLV5r with flags 0 (exported by default before 33). Below 26 it uses plain registerReceiver with no permission.
- So 2.7.2 receives USER_PRESENT on every API level.

3. The platform analysis holds.
- ACTION_USER_PRESENT is sent by SystemUI (KeyguardViewMediator.sendUserPresentBroadcast). SystemUI runs under its own uid, not SYSTEM_UID.
- On API 33+, a NOT_EXPORTED dynamic receiver gets a broadcast only if checkComponentPermission(null, callerUid, ownerUid, exported=false) passes. That check passes only for root/system uid or the app's own uid, so SystemUI's broadcast is dropped as an "Exported Denial".
- On API 24-32, ContextCompat with NOT_EXPORTED attaches the signature-level permission <pkg>.DYNAMIC_RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED_PERMISSION. SystemUI is not signed with the app's key and does not hold it.
- So the receiver never fires. Quick Info does not open after unlock, and the receiver stays registered.

4. It is not a recorded deliberate deviation.
- 11-SUMMARY.md:18 promises "a USER_PRESENT receiver that opens it 300 ms after unlock".
- 11-SUMMARY.md:64 says only the blanket rule "receivers use RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED". That general hardening rule breaks the stated behaviour. It is not a recorded choice to drop the unlock path.

5. Nothing else covers this path. The "Conversation ended" notification still lets the user tap through, but only when notifications are allowed. The automatic open after unlock is lost on every API level.

Severity: major is right. A parity feature is broken on a common path (a call ending while the screen is locked), with no crash or security impact.

Not checked: I did not test this on a device; the conclusion comes from AOSP sender and permission semantics.

confirmed.title: Install/uninstall monitor starts for organic installs; 2.7.2 starts it only for campaign installs
confirmed.detail:
startIfAllowed runs on every MainActivity resume (from GsAppEffects), on boot and on app update. It only checks the overlay permission and iuAlwaysOn, which defaults to true.

2.7.2's IUServiceKeeper and HomeActivity.startIUService first require s9/ao.SJowARcXwM, which is RC enable_gs2_sdk && s9/ao.OoooO(IU). OoooO is the campaign-install gate (Oooo0OO: install_source is not "organic"), the same gate that hides the IU row in Settings.

Here, Settings hides the IU row for organic installs (InstallSource.isCampaign), but the service ignores that gate. Scenario: an organic Play install accepts Home's floating-button offer, which everyone sees on sessions 1/4/7/10 and which grants the overlay permission. That user then gets:
- the ongoing "Monitoring app changes" foreground service, and
- full-screen IU screens launched from the background after every install, update and uninstall.
2.7.2 never shows these to organic users, and Settings gives them no row to turn it off.

GsSetupCardReceiver.handle also skips 2.7.2's matching check (cWbN6pumKk = gs_sdk && OoooO(GS)). Debug builds always count as campaign, so testing does not reveal this.
confirmed.evidence:
PackageMonitorService.kt:132-136 `suspend fun startIfAllowed(...) { ... if (!Settings.canDrawOverlays(app) || !app.preferences.iuAlwaysOn.first()) return; runCatching { ContextCompat.startForegroundService(app, Intent(app, PackageMonitorService::class.java)) } }`
GsPermissions.kt:204-205 `LifecycleResumeEffect(Unit) { scope.launch { PackageMonitorService.startIfAllowed(context) } ...`
SettingsScreen.kt:164 `campaign = InstallSource.isCampaign(context, appPreferences)`; :224 `if (campaign) SettingRow(... R.string.iu_monitoring ...)`
Reference u0/o.Wja3o2vx62 (IUServiceKeeper): if `s9/ao->SJowARcXwM(ctx)` is false it logs "[IUServiceKeeper] not allowed → service not started".
s9/ao.SJowARcXwM = RC gs2_controller.enable_gs2_sdk && OoooO(ctx, bw.IU); Oooo0OO returns install_source != "organic". bw/bf (HomeActivity.startIUService) uses the same gate.
confirmed.fix:
In PackageMonitorService.startIfAllowed, after the overlay check, add `if (!InstallSource.isCampaign(app, app.preferences)) return`. Because the boot receiver, the resume effect and the settings toggle all call this function, all three paths get the gate.

Also add the same early return at the top of the per-event handler in PackageMonitorService.kt (around line 117, next to the iuAlwaysOn check). That covers a service already running from before an upgrade.

At the top of GsSetupCardReceiver.handle, add `if (!InstallSource.isCampaign(app, prefs)) return`. This one is a lower priority.
confirmed.reasoning:
I could not refute the finding. The code and the reference both bear it out.

What the code does now:
- At HEAD, PackageMonitorService.startIfAllowed (lines 135-141) checks only Settings.canDrawOverlays and iuAlwaysOn. The uncommitted working-tree change only adds an IOException guard. Neither version checks InstallSource.isCampaign.
- It is called on every resume, from GsPermissions.kt:204-205 (LifecycleResumeEffect).
- It is also called from IuBootReceiver (PackageMonitorService.kt:150-160, on boot and on update of this app) and from GsSettingScreens.kt:70.
- InstallSource.isCampaign is used only by SettingsScreen.kt:164, PermissionScreen.kt:68 and SplashScreen.kt:72. The service never uses it.
- The 09-SUMMARY (lines 26-27) records the IU row as shown to campaign installs only. No phase summary records ungating the service as a deliberate deviation.
- The Home floating offer (10-SUMMARY:48) runs on sessions 1/4/7/10 and is not campaign-gated, so an organic user can get the overlay permission. iuAlwaysOn then lets the monitor start, and Settings has no IU row to turn it off.

What 2.7.2 does:
- u0/o.smali:137 (IUServiceKeeper) calls s9/ao.SJowARcXwM. Line 279 logs "not allowed -> service not started".
- s9/ao.SJowARcXwM (ao.smali:19065) returns RC gs2_controller.enable_gs2_sdk (default true) AND OoooO(ctx, IU).
- OoooO (ao.smali:14822): for GS/IU it returns true when Oooo0OO (install source is not "organic"). Otherwise it falls back to OoooOO0("organic", IU).
- OoooOO0 returns true for an organic install only when the RC flag organic_ads_enabled is on and the matching organic_user_controller flag is on. Both default to false. With no network, which is this app's case, organic installs are refused.

The reviewer's summary is slightly simplified, because RC can in theory enable IU for organic users. With our offline defaults the result is the same: organic installs never get the service.

On GsSetupCardReceiver: the missing gate is real, but the impact is lower. It also needs afterCallScreenEnabled and the READ_PHONE_STATE permission, and those are normally granted through the GS flow, which is campaign-gated.

- AppPreferences.kt:137-142 calls `AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales`.

The floating-route path is not affected, because `openedFromOutside` is recomputed from the intent at :62-64. No phase summary records this as a deliberate deviation, and 2.7.2 parity is not the question here: this is a lost-state bug in the new code.
